**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ of clause (iv) of P2, the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$, as established in [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the quadratic-form order and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]), the **outcome probabilities** being $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-H calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following conditional-update rule for declared ideal measurements. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(i) Declared measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of a system with state space $H$ consists of a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[def-orthogonal-projection]]) which are mutually orthogonal, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose strong sum is the identity: the finite or norm-convergent countable sum $\sum_{a}P_{a}x=x$ for every $x\in H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]] clause 4). The family is part of the apparatus description; the model does not claim that every laboratory device is a declared measurement of this form.

**(ii) Outcome probabilities.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **probability of the outcome $a$** is $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0$, with $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$; equivalently $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ for a pure preparation $[\psi]$, as in the probability postulate P2. This is the Born law of the declared measurement.

**(iii) Conditional update.** If the outcome $a$ has been recorded and $p_{a}>0$, the preparation posterior to the measurement is
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\,\rho\,P_{a}}{p_{a}},$$
the **Lueders update**. It is a density operator ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]): $P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ is positive, trace class with trace $p_{a}$ by the rank-one series expansion of $\rho$ and the trace formulas, and $\rho_{a}$ is self-adjoint, positive, trace class with trace $1$. The update preserves coherence inside the range of a degenerate $P_{a}$: a superposition of orthogonal vectors within that range is updated to the same relative superposition, and repetition of the same declared measurement on $\rho_{a}$ returns $a$ with probability $1$ (repeatability of the declared projective measurement).

**(iv) Discarded outcomes.** If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the posterior ensemble is
$$\rho'=\sum_{a}P_{a}\,\rho\,P_{a},$$
which converges in trace norm and is a density operator: for an eigen-expansion $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}T_{u_{n},u_{n}}$ as in clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] under the adopted Axiom of Countable Choice, the series $\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}=\sum_{a}\sum_{n}w_{n}T_{P_{a}u_{n},P_{a}u_{n}}$ is nuclear with trace $\sum_{a}\sum_{n}w_{n}\|P_{a}u_{n}\|^{2}=\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$ by the nuclear-series characterization of the trace norm and the absolute convergence of the trace ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]); its normalized form $\rho'$ has the operator dependence recorded by clause (iii) for each branch.

**(v) Limits of the rule.** The rule is an assumption of the model for the declared ideal measurement; it is not derived from the Born law of P2, and it is not asserted for every apparatus. In particular: a measurement of an exact eigenvalue of an operator with continuous spectrum is not represented by normalizing a delta distribution; a photon-absorption detector need not leave an outgoing one-photon preparation of the same form; and a unitary system-apparatus model that produces conditional correlations does not by itself select a unique recorded outcome or resolve which branch occurred. Apparatuses outside the declared class require their own models with their own stated assumptions. The example in [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] that equal finite outcome effects can have different updates is proved there only for finite-dimensional $H$; that example is not a representation result for instruments on infinite-dimensional $H$.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions. They record how the model updates preparations in the declared ideal case and what it deliberately does not claim about arbitrary apparatuses and about the uniqueness of recorded outcomes.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d\ge1$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]), with adjoints as in [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]] and the finite trace as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Recall that an endomorphism $F$ is an **effect** when $F\ge0$ and $I-F\ge0$, i.e. $0\le F\le I$ in the quadratic-form order ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]).

(a) *Definitions.* A finite POVM is a finite family $(F_a)_{a=1}^p$ of effects with $\sum_aF_a=I$. An **instrument** is a finite family $(M_{a,r})_{a,r}$ of endomorphisms of $H$; its outcome effects and updates are $F_a:=\sum_rM_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}$ and $I_a(R):=\sum_rM_{a,r}RM_{a,r}^*$. It is **normalized** when $\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}=I$.

(b) If $(F_a)$ is a finite POVM and $\rho$ a density operator ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]) then $p_a:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)\ge0$ and $\sum_ap_a=1$. If $(M_{a,r})$ is a normalized instrument then the $F_a$ form a finite POVM, $\operatorname{tr}I_a(\rho)=p_a$, each $I_a(\rho)$ is non-negative, and whenever $p_a>0$ the normalized update $I_a(\rho)/p_a$ is a density operator.

(c) *Ideal Lüders case.* For an orthogonal projection $P$ ([[def-orthogonal-projection]]) put $M_0=P$, $M_1=I-P$. Then $\sum_jM_j^*M_j=P+(I-P)=I$, the effects are $F_0=P$, $F_1=I-P$, and $I_j(\rho)=P\rho P$ or $(I-P)\rho(I-P)$.

(d) *Non-determination.* Effects alone do not determine the update: there are two normalized instruments on $\mathbb C^2$ with the same outcome effects $F_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, $F_1=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$ whose updates differ on the same input.

Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 of the framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ be a declared ideal sharp measurement of a system with state space $D(H)$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and let $\rho$ be a state. Then:

**(a) Outcome law.** For every outcome label $a$ the probability is $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$, with $p_{a}\ge0$ and $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$; for the pure state of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$.

**(b) Conditional state and repeatability.** If $p_{a}>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $a$ is the state $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$, with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{b})=0$ for $b\ne a$. Immediate repetition of the same declared measurement therefore returns the same outcome with certainty:
$$\mathbb P(\text{second outcome }b\mid\text{first outcome }a)=\delta_{ab}.$$

**(c) Discarded outcomes.** The discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ is a state and coincides with the outcome-weighted mixture of the conditional states,
$$\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a},$$
the series converging in trace norm; moreover $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ for every $a$ and $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\Phi(\rho)P_{a}$. The conditional-vs-discarded distinction is therefore exactly the distinction between one selected branch $\rho_{a}$ and the mixture of all branches.

**(d) Compatible bounded quantities.** If $B$ is a bounded operator with $P_{a}B=BP_{a}$ for every $a$, then $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)$. In particular, if the declared measurement is the spectral measurement of a bounded assigned sharp observable $A=\sum_{a}a_{a}P_{a}$ (a finite or norm-convergent series with real $a_{a}$), then $A$ commutes with every $P_{a}$ and the mean of $A$ is unchanged by discarding the outcomes.

**(e) Loss of coherence.** If $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal, $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_{1}$, $v\in\operatorname{ran}P_{2}$ for distinct labels $1\ne2$, and $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$, then
$$\Phi(\rho)=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v},\qquad \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Phi(\rho)(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u})\bigr)=0,$$
whereas for the coherent preparation $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u}))=2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta})$: the discarded-outcome ensemble is the classical mixture of the branch states and carries no coherence between the ranges of $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) are conditional on the adopted P3 and on the mathematical items cited; they do not assert that any laboratory apparatus realizes a declared ideal sharp measurement, do not select a unique recorded outcome, and do not describe the disturbance produced by an apparatus outside the declared class (clause (v) of P3). The identification of a device with a declared measurement is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

derivations.claim: [Normalization of the first two instruments] For the first family, $M_{0}^{*}M_{0}=P_{1}^{2}=P_{1}$ and $M_{1}^{*}M_{1}=P_{2}$, so $M_{0}^{*}M_{0}+M_{1}^{*}M_{1}=P_{1}+P_{2}=I$ [F1]. For the second, $M_{0}^{\prime*}=P_{1}W^{*}$ gives $M_{0}^{\prime*}M_{0}'=P_{1}W^{*}WP_{1}=P_{1}^{2}=P_{1}$ because $W^{*}W=I$, and $M_{1}^{\prime*}M_{1}'=P_{2}$; again the sum is $I$. Both families are therefore normalized declared instruments [F2] with the displayed effects $F_{0}=P_{1}$, $F_{1}=P_{2}$ and $F_{0}'=P_{1}$, $F_{1}'=P_{2}$. This is (a).

[Equal outcome probabilities] Since the effects of the two instruments coincide, for every state $\rho$ and each outcome the probability is $p_{0}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{1})$ or $p_{1}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{2})$ with the same value under either instrument [F2]; in particular $p_{0}+p_{1}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{1}+P_{2}))=1$.

[Non-repeatability] For the family of clause (c), $N_{+}^{*}N_{+}=\tfrac12I$ and $N_{-}^{*}N_{-}=\tfrac12B^{2}=\tfrac12I$ by $B^{2}=P_{1}+P_{2}=I$ [F1], so the family is normalized [F2] with effects $F_{+}=F_{-}=\tfrac12I$ and outcome probabilities $\tfrac12,\tfrac12$ in every preparation by [F2]. If the outcome $+$ occurs, the conditional state is $\tfrac12\rho/\tfrac12=\rho$, so the probability that an immediate repetition returns $+$ is again $\operatorname{tr}(\rho\cdot\tfrac12I)=\tfrac12$; if the outcome $-$ occurs, the conditional state is $(\tfrac12B\rho B)/(\tfrac12)=B\rho B$, and the probability that the repetition returns $-$ is $\operatorname{tr}(B\rho B\cdot\tfrac12I)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(B^{2}\rho)=\tfrac12$. Hence the probability of repeating the same outcome is $\tfrac12$ in both cases, not $1$; the declared instrument is not repeatable. This is (c), and it is consistent with the repeatability of the projective case [F4] because $N_{\pm}$ are not projections.

[Different conditional updates] Let $\rho$ be a state with $p_{0}>0$. For the first instrument, $M_{0}\rho M_{0}^{*}=P_{1}\rho P_{1}$, and evaluating in the eigen-expansion of $\rho$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)) or directly by [F1] gives $P_{1}\rho P_{1}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{1})P_{1}=p_{0}P_{1}$; hence the conditional state is $P_{1}=T_{e_{1},e_{1}}$. For the second, $M_{0}'\rho M_{0}^{\prime*}=WP_{1}\rho P_{1}W^{*}=p_{0}WP_{1}W^{*}=p_{0}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ by [F1] and $We_{1}=e_{2}$; hence the conditional state is $T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$. The two updates differ, while step 2.1 gives equal outcome probabilities.

[Different subsequent predictions] The observable $B=P_{1}-P_{2}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projections $P_{1}$ at $+1$ and $P_{2}$ at $-1$, so the probability of the value $+1$ in a preparation $\sigma$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_{1})$. In the conditional state $T_{e_{1},e_{1}}$ of the first instrument this is $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{1},e_{1}}P_{1})=1$ by [F1], and in the conditional state $T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ of the second it is $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{2},e_{2}}P_{1})=|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|^{2}=0$. Thus instruments with the same effects make different predictions for a subsequent measurement, which proves (b).

[Scope] Steps 1.1-5.1 are computations inside the declared instruments of clauses (a) and (c) using the adopted P2(iv) and P3(v) through [F2]; they assert no device behaviour and no outcome uniqueness. This is (d).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.
(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the quadratic-form order and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]), the **outcome probabilities** being $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-H calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ of clause (iv) of P2, the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$, as established in [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $M$ be a closed linear subspace of a real or complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). By the orthogonal-decomposition theorem ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]) every $x\in H$ has a unique representation

$$x=P_Mx+(x-P_Mx),\qquad P_Mx\in M,\quad x-P_Mx\in M^\perp ,$$

and the **Hilbert orthogonal projection onto $M$** is the map

$$P_M:H\longrightarrow M\subseteq H,\qquad x\longmapsto P_Mx ,$$

assigning to $x$ its unique $M$-component. Its defining properties are therefore

$$P_Mx\in M,\qquad x-P_Mx\in M^\perp\qquad(x\in H),$$

which characterise $P_M$ uniquely: a map with these defining properties must agree with the $M$-component of the unique decomposition of each $x$.

**Agreement with the finite-dimensional projection.** If $V$ is a finite-dimensional inner-product space and $W\subseteq V$ a subspace, then [[thm-finite-dimensional-orthogonal-decomposition]] writes $V=W\oplus W^\perp$ and [[def-orthogonal-projection]] defines $P_Wv$ as the unique $W$-component of $v$; the defining properties displayed above are the same, so they define the same map on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.

**Range and kernel.** $P_Mx\in M$ for every $x$, and $P_Mm=m$ for $m\in M$ because $m=m+0$ with $0\in M^\perp$; conversely $P_Mx=0$ says exactly that $x=x-0\in M^\perp$. Hence the range of $P_M$ is $M$ and its kernel is $M^\perp$, and $P_M$ is the identity on $M$ and zero on $M^\perp$.

derivations.claim: [Clause (a)] Put $R_a:=F_a^{1/2}$. For $\psi\in H$, the tensor inner product and $R_a^{*}R_a=F_a$ give $\|W\psi\|^{2}=\sum_a\|R_a\psi\|^{2}=\sum_a\langle F_a\psi,\psi\rangle=\|\psi\|^{2}$, so $W$ is a linear isometry. On elementary tensors, $P_a(\xi\otimes e_b)=\delta_{ab}\xi\otimes e_a$; boundedness and density therefore show that the $P_a$ are orthogonal projections, pairwise orthogonal, and sum to $I$. Finally, for $\psi,\phi\in H$, $\langle W^{*}P_aW\psi,\phi\rangle=\langle P_aW\psi,W\phi\rangle=\langle R_a\psi,R_a\phi\rangle=\langle F_a\psi,\phi\rangle$, so $W^{*}P_aW=F_a$. These are the claims in (a). [given, F1, algebra]

[The dilated state and the outcome probabilities] Write $\rho=\sum_n w_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ by [F3]. The rank-one identities give $WT_{u_n,u_n}W^{*}=T_{Wu_n,Wu_n}$; bounded left and right multiplication preserve trace class and trace-norm limits by [F2], so $\widetilde\rho$ is the trace-norm sum of these positive rank-one operators. Its trace is $\sum_nw_n\|Wu_n\|^{2}=\sum_nw_n=1$ because $W$ is an isometry; positivity follows termwise and is preserved by the operator-norm limit, which follows from trace-norm convergence and [F2]. Thus $\widetilde\rho$ is a state. For each $a$, [F1] gives $P_aWu_n=F_a^{1/2}u_n\otimes e_a$, hence $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho P_a)=\sum_nw_n\operatorname{tr}(T_{Wu_n,Wu_n}P_a)=\sum_nw_n\|F_a^{1/2}u_n\|^{2}=\sum_nw_n\langle F_au_n,u_n\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$, using the trace formula and trace-norm continuity in [F2], the density expansion [F3], and [F8]. This proves (b). [step 1.1, given, F1, F2, F3, F8, algebra]

[The induced conditional state] Assume $p_{a}>0$ and define $J_{a}:H\to H\widehat\otimes C$ by $J_{a}\xi:=\xi\otimes e_{a}$. The tensor-product inner product makes $J_{a}$ an isometry, and the partial-trace rule [F2] gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}(J_{a}XJ_{a}^{*})=X$ for every trace-class $X$, since $J_{a}XJ_{a}^{*}=X\otimes T_{e_{a},e_{a}}$. Directly from the definition of $W$, $P_{a}W=J_{a}F_{a}^{1/2}$. Hence $P_{a}\widetilde\rho P_{a}=J_{a}F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}J_{a}^{*}$, so $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}\widetilde\rho_{a}=F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}/p_{a}$. This is a state because it is the partial trace of the state $\widetilde\rho_{a}$ [F2, F3]. Summing the same identity over $a$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}\sum_{a}P_{a}\widetilde\rho P_{a}=\sum_{a}F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}=\Lambda(\rho)$. The family $M_{a}:=F_{a}^{1/2}$ is normalized because $\sum_{a}M_{a}^{*}M_{a}=\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$; its effects are $F_{a}$ and its conditional updates are exactly the displayed reduced states [F4]. By [F7], $\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda(X))=\sum_a\operatorname{tr}(F_a^{1/2}XF_a^{1/2})=\sum_a\operatorname{tr}(XF_a)=\operatorname{tr}X$ for every trace-class $X$, so $\Lambda$ is trace preserving as stated. This is (c). [step 2.1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, algebra]

[Projective case] If $F_{a}=P_{a}^{\circ}$ is a projection, then $F_{a}^{1/2}=F_{a}$ and $F_{b}^{1/2}F_{a}^{1/2}=P_{b}^{\circ}P_{a}^{\circ}=\delta_{ab}P_{a}^{\circ}$ for the pairwise orthogonal family; hence the induced update of step 3.1 reduces to $P_{a}^{\circ}\rho P_{a}^{\circ}/p_{a}$, the Lueders update [F5]. [step 3.1, given, F5, algebra]

This is a particular choice of instrument associated with the effects; [F6] supplies two normalized declared instruments with the same effects and different updates. Thus the effects alone do not prescribe a unique update among all declared instruments. This is the remaining claim of (d). [step 3.1, given, F6, algebra]

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and for $u,v\in H$ let $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) For every bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]),

$$BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v},\qquad T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v},$$

(b) Let $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class and let $T=\sum_jT_{u_j,v_j}$ be a nuclear representation, i.e. the partial sums converge to $T$ in operator norm and $\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<\infty$ ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]). $$\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\sum_j\langle Bu_j,v_j\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(TB)=\sum_j\langle u_j,B^*v_j\rangle,$$

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ of clause (iv) of P2, the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$, as established in [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. derivations.claim: [The effects and the probabilities] By [F3] each $F_{a}$ is an effect. For a state $\rho$ with expansion [F2], $\sum_{a}p_{a}=\sum_{a}\sum_{n}w_{n}\|M_{a}u_{n}\|^{2}=\sum_{n}w_{n}\|u_{n}\|^{2}=1$ by [F1] with $x=u_{n}$ and $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$; all terms are nonnegative, so the interchange of the sums is legitimate and $p_{a}\ge0$ for each $a$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

[The discarded map and the mixture identity] By [F1] the series $\sum_{a}M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}$ converges in trace norm, its sum $\Phi(\rho)$ is positive trace class with trace $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, and $\Phi$ is trace preserving; hence $\Phi(\rho)$ is a state [F1, F2]. For a label with $p_{a}=0$, [F5] gives $\operatorname{tr}(M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*})=p_{a}=0$, so the positive trace-class summand $M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}$ is $0$; therefore the nonzero summands are exactly those with $p_{a}>0$, and $M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}=p_{a}\rho_{a}$ for them [F5]. Reindexing the trace-norm convergent series gives $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$. This is (a). [step 1.1, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

[Sufficiency of the criterion] Assume $M_bM_a=0$ whenever $b\ne a$. For a state $\rho$ and $p_a>0$, cyclicity and [F5] give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_a F_b)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(M_bM_a)^*(M_bM_a))/p_a=0$ for every $b\ne a$. By clause (a), already proved in steps 1.1-2.1, the outcome probabilities in the state $\rho_a$ sum to $1$, so its probability for $a$ is $1$. Hence the instrument is repeatable, without any assumption that $F_a$ commutes with $M_a$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, given, F1, F5, algebra]

Let $s\in\frac12\mathbb N=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $N:=2s\in\mathbb N$ and let
$V_s:=\mathbb C^{N+1}$ carry the standard inner product
$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k\overline{w_k}$, linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Write $(e_m)_{-s\le m\le s}$ for the standard basis, indexed so that
$e_m$ is the vector with entry $1$ in position $k=s-m$ and entry $0$ elsewhere; thus
$\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=1$ if $m=n$ and $\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=0$ otherwise. Define $\mathbb C$-linear maps
$J_z,J_+,J_-\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_s)$ by their values on this basis ([[def-linear-map]]):

$$J_ze_m:=m\,e_m,\qquad J_+e_m:=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}\,e_{m+1},\qquad J_-e_m:=\sqrt{(s+m)(s-m+1)}\,e_{m-1},$$

where $e_{s+1}:=0$ and $e_{-s-1}:=0$, and put

$$J_x:=\tfrac12(J_++J_-),\qquad J_y:=\tfrac1{2i}(J_+-J_-),\qquad J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2 .$$

Then:

(a) $J_z$, $J_x$ and $J_y$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_s$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), and $J_+^*=J_-$, $J_-^*=J_+$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]);

(b) on $V_s$ the commutators are

$$[J_z,J_+]=J_+,\qquad [J_z,J_-]=-J_-,\qquad [J_+,J_-]=2J_z,\qquad [J_x,J_y]=iJ_z,\qquad [J_y,J_z]=iJ_x,\qquad [J_z,J_x]=iJ_y ;$$

(c) $J^2=J_-J_++J_z^2+J_z=J_+J_-+J_z^2-J_z=s(s+1)I$, and $[J^2,J_z]=[J^2,J_\pm]=0$;

(d) the matrix elements of the raising operator are
$\|J_+e_m\|^2=(s-m)(s+m+1)$ and $\|J_-e_m\|^2=(s+m)(s-m+1)$, and
$\langle J_+e_m,e_{m+1}\rangle=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}$, which is nonzero exactly when $m<s$;

(e) for $s=\tfrac12$, identify $V_{\frac12}=\mathbb C^2$ with the basis ordered as $(e_{\frac12},e_{-\frac12})$ and let

$$\sigma_x:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_y:=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

be the Pauli matrices. Then $J_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ for $i=x,y,z$, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$,
$\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$, and consequently
$\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$ for all $i,j$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ denotes the sign of the permutation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(i,j,k)$.

All statements are finite-dimensional linear algebra: no physical interpretation of $J_x,J_y,J_z$ as angular momentum, and no measurement postulate, is asserted here.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following assignments for identical species and for spin. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(i) Labels and sectors.** For $n$ particles of one species the model forms the $n$-fold completed tensor power $H^{\otimes n}$ of the one-particle space ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose tensor position factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle identities. For a declared **bosonic species** the model uses the symmetric sector $S^{n}H$, the range of the symmetrizing projection $P_{n}^{+}$, and for a declared **fermionic species** the antisymmetric sector $\Lambda^{n}H$, the range of the alternating projection, both as constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. The sector is part of the declared species assignment; the permutation invariance of states in the sector and the resulting exclusion statement for fermions are conditional consequences read off that projection, not assumptions added to it, A bounded quantity $A$ on $H^{\otimes n}$ is restricted to an adopted sector only when it preserves that sector; in particular, $AU_\pi=U_\pi A$ for every permutation implies $AP_n^{\pm}=P_n^{\pm}A$ by the finite projection sums. Bounded tensor maps construct ambient operators; an operator on a single labelled factor need not preserve either sector.

**(ii) Spin.** For a declared **spin label** $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ the model assigns the internal factor $V_s=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ with the standard inner product and basis $(e_m)_{m=-s,-s+1,\ldots,s}$. Here $SU(2)=\{W\in M_2(\mathbb C):W^*W=I_2,\det W=1\}$ with its matrix topology. For $s>0$ put $n=2s\ge1$ and let $F_s:\mathcal S_n\to V_s$ be the unitary identification $F_sv_k=e_{s-k}$ of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]]. The assigned strongly continuous unitary representation is $D_s(W)=F_sU_n(W)F_s^{-1}$. For $s=0$ put $D_0(W)=I_{\mathbb C}$ for every $W$, the trivial one-dimensional representation with zero generators. The spin operators are $S_i=\hbar J_i$ with the self-adjoint endomorphisms of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], satisfying
$$[S_i,S_j]=i\hbar\sum_k\epsilon_{ijk}S_k,\qquad S^2=S_x^2+S_y^2+S_z^2=\hbar^2s(s+1)I.$$
For $A_i(t)=\cos(t/2)I_2-i\sin(t/2)\sigma_i$, the curve $D_s(A_i(t))$ has infinitesimal generator $-iJ_i$, including $s=0$. This specifies the internal $SU(2)$ action. If a spatial Hilbert factor $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is separately assigned a strongly continuous unitary $SU(2)$ representation $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$, the combined action is explicitly $W\mapsto R_{\mathrm{sp}}(W)\otimes D_s(W)$ on $H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_s$: its representation law follows from bounded tensor composition, and continuity follows on elementary tensors and then by density and the unitary norm bound. The existence and physical interpretation of that spatial action require the separate assignment. The spin label and representation are species model assignments; the internal factor is not a rotating body or a spatial coordinate.

**(iii) Species parameters.** The mass, charge, spin label, statistics and any magnetic coupling constant of a species are empirical model parameters: they enter the model as declared values with uncertainty, and no value is derived from the Hilbert-space formalism. The assignment of a sector (symmetric or antisymmetric) to a species is likewise a model assignment, tested through the consequences computed with it.

**(iv) What is not asserted.** The relativistic spin-statistics theorem is not a theorem of this postulate set: the connection between spin and permutation sector adopted here is a nonrelativistic model assignment, and any relativistic statement about it belongs to a framework that adopts relativistic assumptions. Similarly, the postulate asserts nothing about the internal structure, compositeness or interactions of a species beyond the declared parameters.

**(v) Status.** Clauses (i)-(iv) are adopted assumptions of the framework for declared species. They record the sectors and the spin representations used by the model and the empirical status of the species parameters; they make no claim that the model assignment is exact for any species and record no measurement.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ of clause (iv) of P2, the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$, as established in [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 of the framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ be a declared ideal sharp measurement of a system with state space $D(H)$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and let $\rho$ be a state. Then:

**(a) Outcome law.** For every outcome label $a$ the probability is $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$, with $p_{a}\ge0$ and $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$; for the pure state of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$.

**(b) Conditional state and repeatability.** If $p_{a}>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $a$ is the state $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$, with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{b})=0$ for $b\ne a$. Immediate repetition of the same declared measurement therefore returns the same outcome with certainty:
$$\mathbb P(\text{second outcome }b\mid\text{first outcome }a)=\delta_{ab}.$$

**(c) Discarded outcomes.** The discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ is a state and coincides with the outcome-weighted mixture of the conditional states,
$$\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a},$$
the series converging in trace norm; moreover $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ for every $a$ and $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\Phi(\rho)P_{a}$. The conditional-vs-discarded distinction is therefore exactly the distinction between one selected branch $\rho_{a}$ and the mixture of all branches.

**(d) Compatible bounded quantities.** If $B$ is a bounded operator with $P_{a}B=BP_{a}$ for every $a$, then $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)$. In particular, if the declared measurement is the spectral measurement of a bounded assigned sharp observable $A=\sum_{a}a_{a}P_{a}$ (a finite or norm-convergent series with real $a_{a}$), then $A$ commutes with every $P_{a}$ and the mean of $A$ is unchanged by discarding the outcomes.

**(e) Loss of coherence.** If $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal, $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_{1}$, $v\in\operatorname{ran}P_{2}$ for distinct labels $1\ne2$, and $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$, then
$$\Phi(\rho)=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v},\qquad \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Phi(\rho)(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u})\bigr)=0,$$
whereas for the coherent preparation $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u}))=2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta})$: the discarded-outcome ensemble is the classical mixture of the branch states and carries no coherence between the ranges of $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) are conditional on the adopted P3 and on the mathematical items cited; they do not assert that any laboratory apparatus realizes a declared ideal sharp measurement, do not select a unique recorded outcome, and do not describe the disturbance produced by an apparatus outside the declared class (clause (v) of P3). The identification of a device with a declared measurement is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7.
